properties.content:
Report Details

Violation ID: 8259768
Permit API: 051-24464
Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette

Inspection Type: Compliance Schedule Evaluation
Inspection Date: 12/18/2025
Comments: On December 18, 2025, the Department conducted a follow-up inspection to IR 4106474 at the former location of the MAWC well site in Springfield Township, Fayette County. A violation that was issued in IR 4095466 was left outstanding in IR 4106474, for failure to restore the well site by 10/30/2025, in accordance with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 CO and A. The Department requested an NOV Response to IR 4095466 from the operator by December 4, 2025. However, no formal response to IR 4095466 has been received to-date from the operator.The First Modification to the COA was entered on May 1, 2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 CO and A states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites."Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed:The Act 9 sign has been removed from the entrance of the pre-existing access road (photo 1). The access road is to remain unrestored, as it predates construction of the well site (photos 2-4). Temporary stabilization is inconsistent throughout the former well site, as large areas of exposed soil were observed on the slopes at the northern and southern site boundaries (photos 7, 8, 15, and 16). No loose sediment was observed in the rock-lined channels that empty into the pre-existing Sediment Trap (photos 9 and 12). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed at the northern and southern boundaries (photos 9, 11, 17, and 19). The improperly installed super silt fence which was identified in IR 4084771 remains, with the fabric having completely detached and fallen to the ground (photo 18). No evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation was observed on site during this inspection. No restoration plans were found on site during this inspection.The Department continues to recommend that the operator reassess whether the E and S controls installed on site are adequate for this well site restoration.The Department also continues to recommend that the operator apply additional temporary stabilization where bare soil is exposed.Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4095466 shall remain outstanding.

Violation ID: 8186663
Permit API: 033-26494
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Bloom Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/09/2024
Comments: Site inspection conducted on May 9, 2024 regarding a complaint called into the Department of a brine leak. During the inspection I observed a dead spot of vegetation extending approximately 55' long and approximately 16' in the widest spot. The soil was inundated with deer tracks. I used a soil Hanna Groline soil probe to screen for conductivity. All readings exceeded the meters range of 4.00 mS/cm. A small drip was observed coming from the brine tank valve set area. A screw has been inserted into the brine tank to help stop the leak. Fluids still remain within the poly brine tank and the well is active. The Department recommends addressing the brine release. Violations have been cited for the brine release.Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected. Please note, the chart recorder has not been changed in months. The well tag has the previous operators name and contact information listed on. The Department recommends updating the contact information.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/08/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/08/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 8277569
Permit API: 123-47192
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2026
Comments: Evidence of stressed and dead vegetation in the vicinity of the Akins lease tank battery was visible from Rounds Hill Road. Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) and I (Mat Haemer WQS-DEP) were present for this inspection. This inspection was conducted to document findings of an apparent release of production fluids from the Akins tank battery, as well as a separate release from a brine tank previously removed from the nearby Loomis lease's tank battery. Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners previously indicated that he had checked and found the integrity of the Loomis lease brine tank to be sufficient for future use. Kyle indicated that the tank was empty and would be unused until repurposed.The PVC drain line within the secondary containment area of the Akins tank battery was found to be improperly placed. The PVC line straddles the cutout hole in the surface of the brine tank in such a manner that fluids draining through the line would be able to flow over the surface of the brine tank and pool within the secondary containment area. Soil within secondary containment immediately below the PVC line was found to have specific conductance in excess of 17,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Evidence of pooling was visible in the containment area via crude oil staining and stressed vegetation. This indicates that fluid once filled the secondary containment, but apparently was able to migrate downward and/or outward through the secondary containment diking. Stressed and dead vegetation downslope and immediately outside the secondary containment dike further indicates the likelihood that the integrity of the secondary containment is inadequate. Understory vegetation was killed in an area approximately 30 feet wide by 200 feet long. Soils in the killzone were found to have elevated specific conductivity in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.The brine tank staged on location was found to have evidence of stressed and dead vegetation beginning from a point immediately beneath the drain valve and continuing downslope beyond the tank in an area approximately 10 feet wide by 200 feet in length. Specific conductivity in soils below the drain valve measured in excess of 8,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Soils in the killzone downslope of the brine tank were found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with brine disposal receipts for the Akins lease. The Akins Lease Akins 1 OG Well was found to have an illegible ID tag.

Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow up to Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection inspection #4020256 conducted on July 24, 2025 at 0907 hrs. During the inspection, the wellhead and casing strings were visually assessed for signs of leakage, structural deterioration, and or failure. While on-site the well was shut in and not producing. All slam bar holes at the time of inspection were non-detect for combustible gas. As of the completion of this inspection, the operator has not plugged the well nor remedied any of the outstanding violations associated with the well. A previous check valve violation created in error has been closed.

Comments: On 02/21/2020 the Department received a complaint alleging a slide had occurred at the site 3-4 years ago and had not been repaired. Multiple successive slips were observed on the slope south and east of the well pad. Multiple individual scarps and toe bulges were observed. A leak was observed on what appeared to be a pressure vessel valve on the 2MH well. This WQS is requesting OGI follow up.

Comments: Narrative: On 8 June 2020, Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (Department) Water Quality Specialist Mark Madeley (Madeley) and Water Quality Specialist Supervisor Rich Sheriff (Sheriff) conducted a routine/complete inspection (inspection) of the Oakland 11 OG Well (well) in order to determine compliance with the Oil and Gas Act and the applicable technical regulations in 25 Pa. Code Chapters 78 & 102. The following was observed during the Department's inspection: 1. The well was stable and producing, with the pit having been previously reclaimed. The 23 December 2019 inspection of the site indicated that the area was, ‘snow covered and stable…appeared that temporary stabilisation measures will need to be used when weather allows'. 2. Madeley and Sheriff observed a lack of uniform vegetative cover at the site - with no evidence of seed or mulch having been placed. The pit appeared to have deformities as well and was not shaped in such a way as to prevent the pooling of water. 3. Madeley and Sheriff noted the presence of a well permit attached to a nearby tree but no evidence of a site tag on the pump jack or wellhead. 4. Mr James Highhouse arrived on-site during the inspection and told Sheriff and Madeley that he was going to immediately lay mulch about the area. Mr Highhouse also made reference to the presence of a mini-excavator already near the site and said he would be using the machine to grade the pit area for better stabilisation. 5. Sheriff and Madeley expressed their intention to have a look at other wells in the area whilst inspecting and Mr Highhouse said he would be attaching site tags to the Oakland 11 and other nearby pump jacks immediately. Madeley and Sheriff observed Mr Highhouse attaching signs to the Oakland 11 and Oakland 12 (123-48277) pump jacks. The Department has reviewed the observations of Madeley and requests the following information be submitted prior to 17 July 2020: 1. Evidence confirming the pit area has been better shaped to resist pooling of water and erosion See below under REMARKS/VIOLATIONS: PA Code Title 25, Chapter 78.53 & 102.4 (b) (1) and PA Code Title 58, Oil & Gas Act, Chapter 32, 3216 (b): During and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including…producing…the operator shall design, implement and maintain best management practises; [T]he following erosion and sediment control requirements apply…implementation and maintenance of E&S BMPs are required to minimise the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation 2. Evidence confirming mulch has been spread about the area in order to facilitate further vegetative reclamation which will lead to >70% uniform vegetative cover See below under REMARKS/VIOLATIONS: PA Code Title 25, 102.22: Permanent stabilisation. Upon final completion of an earth disturbance activity…top-soil restored, replaced, or amended, seeded, mulched or otherwise permanently stabilised and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation; Clean Streams Law, Section 402 (b) The requested documentation can be faxed to my attention at 814 723 0964, sent via e-mail to mamadeley@pa.gov or posted to the following address: ¿Mark Madeley ¿DEP- Bureau of District Oil and Gas Operations ¿Northwest District -Warren Office ¿321 North State Street ¿Warren, PA 16365 If you have any questions, please contact Mark Madeley at 814 308 3118. Comments: On December 4 2024, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in regards to the spill and associated violations issued under inspection report 3853723.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the Act 9 sign was posted at the access road entrance and the road appeared stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) as well as the Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan (PPC) was in the on site mailbox located at the entrance to the well pad.It appears remediation has begun as soil appears to be excavated from the areas previously identified by the Department and operator to be contaminated. Plastic lining appeared to be placed on all areas of excavation. Temporary erosion and sediment controls appeared installed and functioning correctly downslope of the excavation.The Department was unable to obtain conductivity readings in the areas covered by the plastic lining, however readings were taken just under the lining adjacent to the well head and downslope where no lining was covering the ground. Conductivity readings taken just under the lining adjacent to the well head indicated that not all contaminated material has been removed with readings of 3.17mS, 2.65mS, and 3.14mS. The conductivity reading taken in the area downslope with no plastic lining was 0.25mS, which is comparable to the background reading taken of 0.26mS.Based on the conductivity readings obtained during today's inspection, it does not appear all contaminated materials have been removed from the well site. The Department recommends the operator reassess the well site and ensure all contaminated materials are removed. The Department also recommends the operator ensure the site is properly temporarily stabilized if earth disturbance work ceases for 4 or more days.Based on today's inspection, violations remain outstanding.

Comments: On December 3, 2018, the Department performed an inspection of the CNX RHL22 well pad site, with Kevin Maskol (DEP). Present at time of inspection was Kyle Borden, Spencer Johnson, and Jason Harding (CNX). The site is located in Richhill Twp., Greene County. The inspection was a incident inspection related to a reported reuse water release to the well pad. The operator initially reported a 30 barrel reuse water release to the well pad @ 01:15 a.m. on 12/1/18. The operator did contact the Department at 11:00 a.m. on 12/1/18 to report that the release was greater and was approximately 210 barrels of reuse water. The operator has reported that during the transfer of reuse water from the constructed MASS on the tank pad, along the access road, to the working tanks a communication error occurred and the working tanks were over filled causing a release of approximately 210 barrels of reuse water to the well pad. The reuse water overwhelmed the well pad secondary containment discharging to the well pad and storm water collection channels for the site. The reuse water then entered the PCSM structure discharging off site. The collection channel to the PCSM was also overwhelmed and the water was discharged onto the RHL28 gathering pipeline ROW adjacent to the well pad site. The operator was excavating impacted material off site on the pipeline ROW at time of inspection. The operator was using field conductivity readings to direct the excavation activities. The operator had attempted to plug the PCSM discharge structure, with an inflatable rubber plug, but was unable to do so. Report Details

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 845146
Permit API: 113-20411
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Cherry Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-03-27
Comments: I received at call at 07:30 from Eric Hottenstein of Chesapeake to inform the Department of a release of oil-based drilling mud. He then told me that he would also call the main number to report the spill. I arrived onsite at 09:25 and met with Eric Hottenstein and Nick Krut, both of Chesapeake. We went to observe the release and they described what had occurred. Some newer wells on the pad were recently stimulated and were being set up for flowback. These wells had the intermediate annulus plumbed to a sentry valve (Photo #1). The valves are designed to vent to prevent a build up of pressure. It is believed that the mechanism inside this valve may have become stuck and allowed a build up of pressure causing the top of the valve to come off and release oil-based drilling mud. The area around the wells was partially covered by secondary containment. A section had been removed around the older wells on the site in order to perform maintenance. The unprotected area consisted of both the gravel pad surface and the cement apron around the older wells (Photos #3 & 6). The released drilling mud coated parts of the 105H well, secondary containment, gravel pad, older wells, and cement apron. Eric and Nick believed that a total of 42 gallons of drilling mud was released with 21 gallons on containment and 21 gallons off containment. Before I arrived Mountain Energy was already onsite and had used a Super Sucker to remove the free portion of the drilling mud. They were in the process of power washing the apron and allowing the water/mud mixture to drain into the well cellars (Photo #7). The well heads were going to be washed next with water and degreaser. The well cellars are cement lined and should be sealed to allow the collected water to be vacuumed out. The gravel portion was going to be scraped and excavated as needed. Chesapeake also mentioned pulling back some of the remaining secondary containment to remove and mud that may have seeped underneath. The 105H annulus was connected to a day tank (approx. 350 gallon poly tank) that was in secondary containment. This was a precautionary measure in the event of a second release. Crews were also onsite installing flowback equipment and checking the annulus pressure gauges to monitor the situation. Eric believed the area would be cleaned in about 2 hours. He also mentioned that the day tanks may be installed on other wells in the future to prevent another release. Violations noted.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/02/2024
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 8185764
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/02/2024
Comments: On 5/2/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/completions inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 60 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the site, I met Seneca's Company man, Wesley Sammons who described current operations as follows: The Patterson 801 drilling rig is set up on site drilling production on four of five new wells. This rig arrived on site and started drilling on 3/31/2024. The crew was currently drilling the production section on the 75HU well and were in the process of drilling the curve, currently being at 11,444 feet. The lateral section will follow with the total depth expected to be 25,743 feet. After this well, there are two more to follow with this rig drilling just the production sections. The surface and intermediate sections were previously drilled by a different rig. Wes expects it to take until approximately 6/24/2024 for the rig to finish at the site.Wes accompanied me on the site inspection. The rig and ancillary equipment were stationed on secondary containment. Chemicals were staged on secondary containment. There were 10 frac tanks on the northeast side of the rig staged in secondary containment, these being used for various drilling fluids. There were two frac tanks on the southeast side of the rig that were used to store rainwater collected from the pad surface. This water was being used for drilling fluids. The drill cuttings were being solidified with a plant-based substance called slate dry and with wood pellets prior to being transported offsite to a waste disposal facility. I did witness drill cuttings being piled up above the level of the exterior wall of an open-top tank. I discussed keeping the level of the material low enough to allow for necessary free board. During a previous inspection I witnessed elevated conductance water along the north perimeter berm. I did not witness water in this area during this inspection. Following up on a previous inspection, I collected water sample 9551-108 from the sediment basin near the center overflow inlet box and water sample 9551109 from within the outlet pipe at the corresponding drain grate. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Temporary compost filter socks have been installed throughout the construction site. Vegetation is becoming established in recently constructed areas but the requirements for permanent stabilization have not been met yet. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Infiltration berms 2 and 3 and the sedimentation basin do not yet meet the vegetative requirements for permanent stabilization.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3724668 and ID 3736567 for a 6' x 60' puddle of water with elevated conductance and with a white substance in it; discovered on the unprotected pad surface and flowing into the sediment basin during drilling operations. The DEP recommends the following: 1. Prevent water with elevated levels of aluminum from leaving the pad surface, from entering the sediment basin, from leaving the LOD and from infiltrating into the groundwater. 2. Continues the process of determining the source of contamination as witnessed in this and prior inspections. 3. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad and entering the sediment basin. Clean and report as necessary.4. Maintain adequate levels of freeboard in open-topped containers including the half-round dumpsters being used for drill cuttings.5. Continue to monitor the stability and functionality of the sediment traps and sediment basin and repair as necessary.I left the site at 1110 hours.

Comments: On March 11, 2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of the Gabonay National City Bank 6 well in response to the operator's submission of a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well. This inspection is being separated into 3 inspection reports due to the number of photos taken. The narrative of all 3 inspection reports are identical except for the references to photos. This is inspection report 1 of 3.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, plugging operations have not yet commenced and there is currently no rig on-site. Earth disturbance for site preparation has commenced. E and S plan is present on-site at the mailbox at the beginning of the access road.Well is tagged and posted. Production tank is observed within an adequately vegetated berm at this time. No spills, leaks, or releases are observed at this time. The RCE is not installed as depicted on the plans. Minimal gravel is observed, which appears to be pre-existing. The access road does not appear to be graveled by the operator despite the E and S plans calling for the road to be "graveled as necessary." Four locations on the access road are experiencing erosion and sedimentation off of the access road (Photos 10-13, 18). CFS is also not observed in these locations despite the E and S plan call for CFS installed "as needed."There are 8 culvert crossings observed during today's inspection. Some ends of the culverts are blocked due to what appears to be recent soil and vegetation clearing off the access road. Some of the culvert crossings appear to possibly be stream crossings. A follow up inspection is being requested with Department Biologists to identify possible streams and/or wetlands. CFS is not observed to be installed at any of the culvert crossings except for the last culvert crossing closest to the site. The CFS at this crossing appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time, but is only installed on one side of the crossing. The E and S plans on site do not delineate or identify any stream or wetlands or crossings of any streams or wetlands, and no 105 permits are observed on site or at any of the crossings at this time. The Department recommends the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan.CFS is observed to be installed on-site near the well and appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time. The location of the CFS appears to be placed in the correct area in relation to the site's topography, however the E and S plans depict the CFS to be placed on the opposite (East) side of the site. A small channel of stormwater appears to be leaving the site and passing through CFS at this time, however no sediment is observed leaving the site. The Department recommends the operator monitor and maintain this area as necessary to ensure CFS continues to function properly. Plastic matting is observed to be installed in 3 locations along the access road.The Department recommends the operator redline the site plans to appropriately match on-site field changes.Violations are being issued for accelerated erosion and sedimentation off of the access road, for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, and for failing to maintain access road culverts. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending consultation with Department Biologists.

Comments: This inspection was performed following a report from the operator of a brine leak at the tank battery of the #38448 well location (CID #355324). It appears as though ice accumulated within the diking and dislodged the drain line from the stock tank to the brine tank, allowing the tank to drain into the diking. properties.content:

Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford

Inspection Date: 4/02/2026
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's Lee North well pad (1H expansion) located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/2/2026 at 1025 hours. The weather was 44 degrees F with cloudy skies and light rain. A Blackhill Energy representative accompanied me during the inspection. On 3/6/2026, the DEP noted violations due to sediment laden fluids having been observed escaping the site's limit-of-disturbance (LOD) and impacting Wetland 4J located downslope of the stormwater control basin's outlet pipe. Additional information regarding the inspection from 3/6/2026 can be seen in inspection record #4154382. Blackhill Energy responded to the violations noted on 3/6/2026 by having the construction contractor install additional filter sock around the outlet pipe. The additional controls were installed within a few hours of the DEP notifying Blackhill Energy of the findings. On 3/9/2026, the construction contractor returned and installed a rock outlet apron and additional filtration measures around the discharge point. During this inspection, recent rainfall has added additional sediment laden fluids into the stormwater control basin. The skimmer pipe that flows fluids from the basin into the outlet box was not functioning as designed (photo #6). As seen in photo #6, sediment laden fluids were directly entering the outlet box from around the skimmer pipe. The controls added below the basin's outlet pipe were observed to be overtopping with sediment laden fluids (photos #5, 7 and 9). The sediment laden fluids were observed escaping the site's LOD and entering wetland 4J (photo #8). A representative with the construction contractor took a look at the skimmer outlet pipe and explained that they could try to temporarily grout around the pipe within the outlet box to prevent fluids from entering the box before going through the skimmer. The construction contractor and Blackhill Energy both explained that additional controls would be added to the area below the basin's outlet pipe to help contain sediment laden fluids to the well site.Based on the findings of this inspection report and the continued release of sediment laden fluids outside of the site's LOD and into Wetland 4J, the violations cited against API #015-24012 on 3/6/2026 remain outstanding at this time.I departed the site at 1200 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-05-29 to Bkv Opr Llc in Washington Twp, Wyoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Bkv Opr Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation ID: 851856
Permit API: 131-20585
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Washington Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-05-29
Comments: I arrived at the site at 10:34 in response to a reported spill incident of an unknown volume of a fluid substance spilled to the pad surface, and into stormwater in a site perimeter ditch. The weather conditions are partly cloudy skies, breezy, warm and humid, with temperatures in the low to mid 70's. Representing the Department during the inspection in addition to myself include Ken Kennedy, Eric Miller, Cassidy Moyer and Eric Rooney. Marvin Schellie, consultant of BKV, is the company man at the site. Representing BKV is Tom Weller, Matt Knight and Dale Bennett. Representing the BKV consultant Apex Environmental is Shelly Bowen, and Jamie Moran. Kevin Brady of Whitetail Environmental, a BKV consultant, is also at the site. The current drilling depth on the Reynolds 2H well is (3,096) feet. Air drilling is in progress. The intermediate casing was cemented on 5/27/19 according to Mr. Schellie. Mr. Weller explained that inadvertently, a bypass valve for an overflow line was left open on the Iron Horse shale gas separator. Following waiting on cement (WOC), displacement fluid was being unloaded from the intermediate casing, and the existing separator tank was half full. When changed over and pressuring up to resume air drilling, air and some remaining displacement fluid was inadvertently discharged across the open top tank under pressure, and overflowed the tank and containment. Mr. Weller estimated that less than (1) barrel (42) gallons, was released off containment. Mr. Weller explained that the displaced water was recycled from previous air drilling operations, which may include the use of various lube products, and air foaming and defoaming products. Mr. Brady provided the Department with Safety Data Sheets (SDS) of the products. The SDS indicates the chemical name for the lube product is ECO Drill 100, with biodegradable drill oil listed as a synonym. The SDS indicates the foaming product is FoamFresh, with Eco-Friendly Foamer listed as a synonym. Mr. Brady also provided the Department with photos of the source of the fluid spilled out of the container, the ditch which is labeled stormwater channel, and a map of the site. The container is located on secondary containment in the area on the pad surface termed the backyard by BKV. This particular area is located adjacent to the drilling rig and site perimeter berm. Mr. Brady informed the Department that he recorded specific conductance (conductivity) of (4) millisiemens/cm in water in the stormwater channel on 5/28/19 at 15:35, (145) parts per million in chlorides on a Hach test strip on 5/28/19 at 15:35, and a sump was constructed in the channel as a result of the elevated readings. He further stated that an on-site vacuum truck was immediately deployed to the area where the spill occurred, and an additional vacuum truck was dispatched to remove impacted stormwater in the channel. Apex informed the Department they screened the impacted area on the ground surface with a photoionization detector (PID) meter for the potential presence of volatile organic compounds at 8:24 AM today, 5/29/19, and screened the water in the channel for conductivity at 8:40 AM today, 5/29/19. Apex indicated they excavated small holes in (3) locations on the berm where the impact occurred, to obtain PID readings. The reading at the first location was (1.9) ppm; the second location was (1.6) ppm, and the third location was 1.5 ppm. The PID meter read (0) parts per million on containment near the tank as part of the release. Conductivity was (306) microsiemens/cm. I used a Hanna HI 98331 Groline Soil Test meter, and an Oakton PCTS 50 meter to record conductivity of water in the channel. During the inspection, the Department and Apex collected samples of stormwater in the channel in (3) separate locations. The Department also collected a sample of fluid in the container associated with the spill. See photos. The Department left the site at 13:28.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/21/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 989364
Permit API: 015-23708
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/21/2023
Comments: On 3/21/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident - response to an accident or event inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. On 3/18/2023 Chesapeake reported that 10 gallons of produced water sprayed out of a damaged pipe on a GPU unit, the water impacting the unprotected pad surface. Creston Environmental identified the extent of the impacted area and excavation was scheduled for 3/20/2023. It was 39 degrees and clear when I arrived on location.When I first arrived at the site, I met Chesapeake's Pat Adams who described activities with the event. Pat showed me a pipe nipple on the 1HC GPU that had been replaced. He showed me the excavated area that is in the northeast corner of the site. The excavated hole had not been backfilled at the time of the inspection. The excavated area is roughly 12' x 40' with various depths up to 2', running along the edge of the perimeter berm. The GPU had been moved from the affected area and had not been returned back to its original position. Pat said that a truck driver first witnessed the spill. Upon discovery, all ten wells were shut in. Pat had just put the 9 unaffected wells back into production before my arrival. The 1HC was still shut in until the GPU is reinstalled. The excavated material remains on site and has been piled on a plastic sheet on the southeast corner of the pad. I field tested some small water puddles in the bottom of the excavated area with results being as high as 4.18 mS conductance. Using a Hanna Gro-line soil probe, I probed the side of the excavated area with one reading being 1.03 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance of the water and soil with Chesapeake's Eric Hottenstein. Eric said he would have someone probe the excavated area to determine if further excavation was necessary. Eric also reported that it was their practice not to fill in the excavated area until they had gotten confirmation samples back. Danielle Schaad met me on location before I left and we discussed the elevated conductance areas. She said that they would excavate some more of the area as determined by the results of field tests.There were nine wells staged for production and one offline at the time of the inspection. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. Six of the GPUs and the production tank had secondary containment. Water in the 101HC GPU secondary containment field tested at 4.55 mS conductance. There are seven frac tanks on site along with one gas buster that were located in secondary containment. Pat reported that the wells were sending their production fluid directly to the production tank. He said the frac tanks were not being used but were still on site in case of inclement weather.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Temporary stabilization was noted on the east perimeter berm. PCSM is addressed by two retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 57(a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b). Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3459318 for the spill of brine fluid outside of secondary containment.The DEP recommends the following:1. Screen the area impacted by the release of production fluid for additional contaminants and continue with the excavation as determined by the screening results.2. Remove the water in the 101HC GPU secondary containment at the earliest convenience.I left the site at 1335 hours.

Report Details

Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8201132
Permit API: 059-25626
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Center Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/11/2024
Comments: On 9/11/2024, I conducted a follow-up inspection of the Kentor Well Pad following violations issued on 9/9/2024 for a produced fluid spill proceeding the plugging of the Kentor 8H Well (Inspection ID: 3826729, Enforcement ID). Staining as a result of produced fluid spilling onto the Kentor Well Pad was discovered on 9/6/2024 following the removal of secondary containment used in the Kentor 8H Well plugging process. Leatherwood LLC was the Operator responsible for the spill, however EQT took responsibility for spill remediation. EQT is following Act 2 cleanup protocols as it is still unknown how much produced fluid was spilled.On site at the time of inspection was SPSI and Moody and Associates. I spoke to SPSI who confirmed that the spill had originated from the secondary containment during the Kentor 8H well plugging process, however it was still unclear how much produced fluid was spilled. A hole dug near the beginning of remediation approximately 75-100 feet from the plugged well yielded in produced fluid seeping into the hole. At the time of inspection, I observed produced fluid sitting within the excavated hole. SPSI stated that they were waiting for the arrival of Moody and Associates to proceed with remediation because the origin of the remaining produced fluid was unknown.While on site I observed the following:-Leatherwood LLC and EQTs Act 9 signs were posted at the site entrance (Photos 1-2).-Discoloration in the aggregate on site was apparent where excavation and impacted material remediation occurred (Photos 3-4).-The hole excavated by SPSI early in remediation was still seeping produced fluid at the time of inspection. It was undetermined where the produced fluid was seeping from and how much remained on site that was unaccounted for. I observed high conductivity of the fluid sitting in the hole (9.20 mS/cm), and the soil below the fluid was slightly elevated but below 3 mS/cm (Photos 7-11).-Previously stained aggregate located approximately 15 feet from the excavated hole demonstrated normal conductivity, and the top layer of aggregate appeared to be scraped off (Photo 12).-The plugged Kentor 8H well was barricaded by concrete barriers and backfilled since previous inspection. I observed normal conductivity readings in areas around the concrete barriers that were previously elevated (Photos 13-18).-Rolloff boxes were staged on site with impacted material. Boxes were being hauled off site at the time of inspection (Photo 19).-A ditch installed left of the plugged well was holding rainwater at the time of inspection (Photo 20).Because an unaccounted amount of produced fluid is still seeping from the Kentor Well Pad into the excavated hole approximately 75-100 feet from the origin of the spill, violations of 91.34(A), 78a.57(a), 78a.54 and SWMA 301 remain outstanding. Additionally, The Department is requesting a copy of the Kentor 8H well plugging secondary containment plan and all maintenance and inspection records associated with the secondary containment used in the plugging process.

The well remains abandoned and is not plugged. - The violation of 78.88(a) for failing to submit annual MIA reports remains outstanding. - The violation of 78.121(a) for failing to submit production reports remains outstanding. - The violation of 78.73(a) for failing to repair the existing leak on the well head remains outstanding. - The violation of OGA3220(a) for failing to plug the well upon abandoning it remains outstanding. - An Order to plug this well was issued by the Department on 12/12/2019, however the well remains abandoned and is not plugged. The Operator has failed to comply with the conditions set forth in the Order and is therefore in violation of OGA3259(1).

Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted to assess conditions in the area of the produced water spill reported to the Department on 2/17/20. DEP Compliance Specialist Chris Southard accompanied me on this inspection. Water continues to pool in front of the two produced water tanks. The puddle in front of the north produced water tank, where the spill occurred, had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 6.08 mS/cm. In the puddle in front of the south produced water tank the EC was approximately 1.7 mS/cm. It appeared that some additional gravel was applied since the previous inspection 2/18/20. It was not clear whether any additional excavation had been done. There was no evidence that the south tank had been moved. It did not appear that there was any excavation done or new gravel placed beneath the south tank. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation for this release. The Department recommends moving the south tank and screening the pad surface for electrical conductivity, excavating impacted material necessary. Outstanding violations.
